subject.title: sessions_send blocked by visibility guard even when a2a policy allows cross-agent messaging

question: Should cross-agent `sessions_send` be allowed under `tools.sessions.visibility="tree"` when `tools.agentToAgent` explicitly allows the requester and target, or should this wait for a broader granular visibility policy?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair intentionally changes the boundary between message injection and transcript/session visibility, which needs maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
options.body: Allow cross-agent `send` to use A2A policy as the authority while requiring tests and proof that list, history, status, and sandbox spawned scopes remain restricted.

options.title: Fold Into Granular Visibility
options.body: Route implementation through the broader per-capability visibility design so one public config model owns send/read/list/status separation.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Continue requiring `visibility="all"` for cross-agent sends and document that tradeoff as intentional until a larger policy lands.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
recommendation.body: Allow cross-agent `send` to use A2A policy as the authority while requiring tests and proof that list, history, status, and sandbox spawned scopes remain restricted.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal points to this owner for the sandbox visibility and session access helper architecture that would need to change.
